title: Prefill-probe routing and graceful fallback policy for speculative decoding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a probe-based prefill routing layer in the serving runtime that selects and verifies lightweight candidate models for speculative decoding. This ticket ties prefill probe outcomes into acceptance metrics, kernel selection hints, and a deterministic fallback policy to ensure SLOs are preserved when speculative candidates under-perform. The goal is to reduce median/ tail latency for common prompt shapes while maintaining accuracy/regression guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end flow that issues a prefill probe to one or more candidate models prior to full decode and records acceptance decision within 100ms overhead
Acceptance metric defined: probe_similarity >= 0.92 OR token-agreement >= 0.90 across benchmark prompt set
When probe indicates accept=false, runtime falls back to primary full model without impacting request correctness or losing KV cache state
Integration with kernel selection: when a candidate is accepted, runtime routes decode to the candidate's preferred kernel path and records kernel-tagged telemetry
Perf target: p50 token latency reduced by >=10% on internal harness for selected workloads; no more than 2% regression in quality metrics vs baseline
Unit + integration tests for probe logic, acceptance threshold edge-cases, and fallback code paths
Canary rollout with tracing and alerting hooks (false-accept rate alarm > 0.5%)
implementation_plan: Add lightweight prefill-probe RPC and proto to runtime API
Implement probe scoring: approximate-L2 on embeddings + token-overlap heuristic
Wire probe output to acceptance policy module with tunable thresholds
Propagate kernel hint from candidate metadata into kernel-selection layer
Ensure KV cache reuse/transfer when switching from probe to full-decode or fallback
Add telemetry: probe_duration_ms, accept_decision, probe_score, false_accept_flag, kernel_tag
Backfill unit tests and e2e harness; run distributed load tests against canary cluster
tradeoffs_and_rejects: Rejected aggressive multi-probe approach: issuing >2 probes increases overall overhead and destabilizes p95 latency under load
Considered embedding-based single-threshold only; rejected because token-level agreement catch subtle output regressions
Deliberately delayed dynamic thresholding feature (adaptive per-customer) to a follow-up as it requires RBAC and billing changes

2026-03-13: Implemented probe RPC signature and basic scorer. Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2487
2026-03-13: Blocker noted: KV cache migration between probe and decode needs safe checkpoints to avoid double-insert. Investigating two options (incremental copy vs pointer swap).
qa_tasks: Create replay harness with 10M recent production requests and run candidate vs baseline comparisons
Define failure injection tests: drop probe results, slow probe RTT, probe false-accept simulation
Verify KV cache consistency after fallback under high concurrency
Smoke test kernel-tag propagation on CPU/GPU and quantized runtimes
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature flag off in runtime builds; smoke tests in staging
Stage 1: Canary on 1% of hosted traffic for low-risk customers; monitor false_accept_rate and user-facing error rates
Stage 2: Expand to 10% after 48h if alarms are green; enable per-model gating
Stage 3: Full rollout to hosted with release runtime-1.23; provide toggle for Dedicated customers
Fallback policy: immediate failover to primary model when probe_accept=false OR probe_timeout > 200ms
